# /crav1-finalize-commit

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [From commit to merge](../../from-commit.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-finalize-commit/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Draft the commit message, then commit, copy, change, or stop.

**[`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md)** always drafts first, then offers commit, copy, change, or stop (1.83.0; there is no opening question). When no style rule is saved, it drafts in the recommended style and asks CRAV1 style or git log in the same prompt as those choices (1.89.0), at most once per run (1.90.5). `message only` drafts with no commit, the same as copy, and a headless run with no choice word ends as copy. It replaces draft-commit-message; its rules are kept as a branch.

Only write the message (was `/crav1-draft-commit-message`): Paste-ready Summary/Description for any git client; CRAV1 style or live git log, once or onward (deletable rule); does not commit unless they ask. Optional Azure Boards mention from `docs/specs/<slug>/work-item.md` is the last description line.

Commit (was [`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md)): Same draft, then **commit first**, then copy for your git client, change (edit or rewrite), or stop (no push). Keeps that mention through the HEAD check and the strip of the known tool trailers it did not write (the list in `references/tool-trailers.md`: Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Aider, Codex, Gemini, Jules, Devin and more); `Signed-off-by` and a real person's `Co-authored-by` stay (1.94.0).

Trailer hook (1.90.0): asked once per repo in the same prompt, "Strip tool trailers on every commit for this repo?". `strip trailers` writes a committed `.githooks/commit-msg` (POSIX sh) that removes only the known tool trailers in `references/tool-trailers.md`, runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, and saves the answer in a `trailer-hook` rule. `Signed-off-by` and human `Co-authored-by` lines stay. A teammate whose repo has the hook but not the config gets the config line on their first run, with no question. `keep trailers` saves no and never asks again.

Fetch, pull and check (1.81.0): after the commit it fetches. When the branch is behind its upstream it pulls with a merge (`git pull --no-rebase`, never a rebase) and resolves conflicts in specs, system files and notes by the kit's rules: both sides' added lines kept, ours first; the newest `Synced at` entry per branch; note indexes rebuilt with `notes_index.py`. Before the merge commit it checks that no line either side added is missing. One question only when the two sides say different things about the same fact: keep both (a `**Conflict:**` line), mine, theirs, or stop. Code file conflicts stay with you. When not behind, it checks any unpushed merge, including one made by hand, and offers to restore dropped lines; restored lines go into this run's commit (1.91.0). `pull` does this with no commit first. It never pushes; it ends with `Ready to push.`

## Choice words

Exact words for bots and scripted runs (no `--flags`). A word in the invocation takes that choice without asking. A headless or bot run with no word stops and names the valid words.

| Question | Word | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Commit or message | `commit` | the same as commit now (1.76.1) |
| Commit or message | `message only` | draft and show, no git commit; the same as copy (1.83.0) |
| Commit or message | `commit now` | draft, show, then commit with no choice question (never pushes) |
| Pull | `pull` | fetch, then the pull path or the nothing-lost check, with no commit first (1.81.0) |
| Style | `crav1` | CRAV1 style, this commit only |
| Style | `git log` | match git log, this commit only |
| Trailer hook | `strip trailers` | add the shared .githooks/commit-msg hook that strips known tool trailers, and save yes (1.90.0); on commit, the hook and its project rule go into that commit (1.90.6) |
| Trailer hook | `keep trailers` | no hook; save no so it is not asked again (1.90.0) |

## Runs when

You want the commit message, or the commit itself. Called by the user and by [`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md).

## Prompts

Prompt budget: 3 (the most prompts in one run, the closing yes included). A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: Only write the message: The diff, recent git log, and `work-item.md`; Commit: The same commit inputs as draft.

Only write the message: Reads the staged or unstaged diff, recent `git log`, an existing persist rule, and `work-item.md` when it exists. The mention picks the id whose milestone or slice label matches the slice being worked, asks when that is unclear, and still reads a single unlabeled line. Commit: Reads the same commit inputs through draft.

## Writes

In short: Only write the message: A host persist rule when onward is chosen; a commit only when also asked in that turn; Commit: The persist rule when onward is chosen, and the git commit when picked.

Only write the message: Writes a host persist rule only when the user chooses onward. Commit: Writes the persist rule when onward is chosen, and the git commit when the user picks commit. When behind, a merge commit from the pull path, with kit-file conflicts resolved and note indexes rebuilt (1.81.0).

## Does not

Only write the message: Leaves the git commit alone. Commit: Leaves push alone.

Limits and exceptions: Only write the message: commits only when the user also asked to commit in that turn. Commit: the worker commits immediately and skips the menu.

## You run next / Runs by itself

- You run next: [`/crav1-open-pr`](crav1-open-pr.md)
- Runs by itself: Only write the message: Calls no skill. Commit: Calls [`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md).
